body_markdown:
Let’s face it, there’s a lot on the line when it comes to anything involving automobiles. It could be something like racing for pink slips. It could be a multi-million-dollar deal in a conference room situated in Metro Detroit. Heck, it could even be a nail-biter of a race televised internationally, an event where prestige and power hang in the balance.


There are probably more automotive rivalries out there than anyone can possibly fathom. That’s why I decided to ask our readers for their favorite example of the genre. The one that sticks in my mind the most is that of Dale Earnhardt and Jeff Gordon. That’s something I hate to admit, as I generally like automotive racing for the vehicles, not the drama associated with the series they participate in. So instead, let me kick things off with a classic rivalry in the corporate sector.


## Lee Iacocca vs. Henry Ford II


Ford


Ford


The story is likely more complicated than we will ever know, but there’s no doubt that Henry Ford II and Lee Iacocca weren’t the best of friends. Henry Ford II had the Herculean task of taking over his grandfather’s company, which he reinvented by knocking down organizational walls put up by the first Henry Ford. He hired outsiders, including the famous Whiz Kids, to turn around the company. And Iacocca made his own mark on the company, looking to innovate with cars like the Mustang and the minivan-like[Ford Carousel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Carousel) . He set up Lincoln for 20+ years of personal luxury sales success with the Continental Mark III, and the controversial Pinto and Mustang II were no slouch in the sales department, either.


Yet the two successful executives couldn’t stand each other. It’s a rivalry with no flashy ending, only a long-forgotten firing way back in 1978. Henry Ford II’s legacy was cemented by his decades of accomplishments, removing larger-than-life legacies from the car-making equation. Iacocca wasn’t ready to rest on his laurels, and took the Ford Carousel concept with him to Chrysler. It found a rather fantastic home on the K-car platform and earned untold dollars in profit, just like how the Mustang took off with Falcon DNA inside it.


This really isn’t about a winner or loser, as both gentlemen were victorious in my book. So this is a good time to hand things off to you, dear reader. Because I would like to know…


**What’s Your Favorite Automotive Rivalry?**
